recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Divide by √(a²+b²)
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the move that makes the whole family work. Dividing by √(a²+b²) forces the two coefficients to become a cosine and a sine of the same angle, so the left side collapses to ONE trig function.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by √(a² + b²) = 2. That forces both coefficients to become a sine and a cosine of one angle.

recall.must_convey: That both sides are divided by √(a²+b²) = 2, so the coefficients become √3/2 and 1/2.

steps.why: a sinθ + b cosθ can never be solved directly, but divided by √(a²+b²) its coefficients always become the cosine and sine of some angle — and then one compound-angle formula finishes it.
common_mistakes: Dividing by a + b instead of √(a²+b²).

steps.label: Recognise the standard angles
steps.margin_note: Second mark. √3/2 is cos30° and 1/2 is sin30°, so the left side is exactly the sin(A−B) pattern. The right side, 1/√2, is sin45°.
steps.memory_tip: √3/2 is cos 30° and 1/2 is sin 30° — that way round. The right side 1/√2 is sin 45°.

recall.must_convey: That √3/2 = cos30°, 1/2 = sin30° and 1/√2 = sin45°, matching the sin(A−B) pattern.

match the values to known angles

steps.why: The two coefficients always square-and-add to 1 after the division, which is exactly the condition for them to be a cosine and a sine of one angle.
common_mistakes: Matching √3/2 to sin30° instead of cos30°.
Writing 1/√2 as cos45° and then using the wrong formula.

steps.label: Collapse to one function
steps.margin_note: Third mark. sinA cosB − cosA sinB is sin(A−B), so the equation becomes a single sine equal to a single sine. The principal value is then read off directly.
steps.memory_tip: sinA cosB − cosA sinB = sin(A − B), so the angle is θ − π/6 and the principal value is π/4.
lines: Here the principal value is α = π/4

recall.must_convey: That the left side becomes sin(θ − π/6) and the principal value is π/4.

steps.why: Once the equation reads sin(something) = sin(α), the general solution formula applies mechanically. Getting to that form is the whole difficulty.
common_mistakes: Using sin(A+B) and getting θ + π/6.
Taking the principal value as π/6.

steps.label: Write the general solution
steps.margin_note: Last mark. For a SINE equation the general solution is nπ + (−1)ⁿα. Solve for θ, and leave the answer with n ∈ Z — an equation like this has infinitely many solutions.
steps.memory_tip: For a SINE equation it is nπ + (−1)ⁿα. Add the π/6 back, and write n ∈ Z.

steps.why: Sine, cosine and tangent each have their own general solution formula, and using the wrong one is the commonest error in the chapter. Sine gets nπ + (−1)ⁿα.
common_mistakes: Using the cosine form 2nπ ± α for a sine equation.
